programs.name: Advanced Computing BAdvComp (Computer Science specialisation)
programs.a_level_offer: GCE A Levels aggregate 15 from three A2 subjects (or 16 from four), with A*=6, A=5, B=4, C=3, D=2, E=1; AS subjects not counted (2027 entry, indicative).
programs.ib_offer: IB Diploma total of 34 points (2027 entry, indicative).
programs.ap_offer: US High School Diploma with GPA 3.2 and at least three AP exams (maximum four considered; only scores of 3 or higher count, Calculus AB subgrade excluded): aggregate 13 from three APs or 16 from four; or SAT 1340 / ACT 28 with completed high school (APs scoring 3 or better can lower the SAT/ACT needed).
programs.required_subjects: Assumed knowledge: Mathematics Extension 1 (NSW HSC level). The page also shows a Mathematics prerequisite (Band 4 in HSC Mathematics Advanced or the equivalent) and links to a check of whether it applies to your qualification.
programs.toefl_note: TOEFL iBT 85 overall with at least 17 in Reading, Listening and Speaking and 19 in Writing (old 0-120 scale; the page gives no 1-6 scale score). Only the TOEFL Australia version on the 0-120 scale is accepted. PTE Academic 64 overall and 60 in each band.
programs.english_note: Course page: IELTS 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each band, or TOEFL iBT 85 / PTE 64. Applies if English is not your first language and you have not completed qualifying study in English.
programs.notes: 2027 entry, Semester 1 (February) and Semester 2 (August) intakes. The Bachelor of Advanced Computing is Sydney's main computing degree (Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Software Development or Computational Data Science specialisations); the BSc with a Computer Science major is not covered here. Entry values come from the course page set to 'International student, 2027': entry score 90.0 ATAR (indicative, a guide and subject to change), fee A$63,600 (page says estimate only, year 1 of 48 credit points). The qualification scores (IB 34, GCE 15/16, AP 13/16/3.2, SAT 1340, ACT 28) are the page's 'Find your qualification' data. The deadline is the general international undergraduate closing date for Semester 1: 1 December 2026 (page https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/applying/application-dates.html, which says to check the course page and apply early). Apply directly or through an authorised agent; UAC is mandatory only for current Australian Year 12 students or IB students in Australia. AP route: same course page.

Bachelor of Economics is in the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences (CRICOS 003336G); economics majors inside the Bachelor of Commerce are not covered here. Entry values come from the course page set to 'International student, 2027': entry score 85.0 ATAR (indicative, a guide and subject to change), fee A$59,100 (estimate; page says year 1 of 48 credit points). The qualification scores (IB 31, GCE 14/14, AP 12/15/3.2, SAT 1300, ACT 26) are the page's 'Find your qualification' data. Deadline: general international undergraduate closing date for Semester 1, 1 December 2026 (page https://www.sydney.edu.au/study/applying/application-dates.html; apply early). Apply directly or through an authorised agent; UAC is mandatory only for current Australian Year 12 students or IB students in Australia. AP route: same course page.
